intro: Makes free and compulsory elementary education (Class 1–8) a right for every child aged 6–14, under Article 21A of the Constitution. Also requires private schools to reserve seats for disadvantaged children.

sections.p: Every child aged 6–14 has the right to free education in a neighbourhood school until Class 8. No fees or charges can stop a child from attending.

Private unaided schools (except minority institutions) must admit children from weaker and disadvantaged sections in at least 25% of entry-level seats, free of cost. The government reimburses the school. In Tamil Nadu, applications are made online through the school education department each year.
Schools can't charge capitation fees or interview or test children or parents for admission.
sections.pen: Capitation fee: fine up to 10 times the fee. Screening: ₹25,000 first, ₹50,000 after

sections.p: A child can't be denied admission for lack of a birth certificate or other age proof, or because the academic year has started.

Earlier, no child could be held back until Class 8. Since a 2019 amendment, schools may hold back students in Class 5 and 8 if they fail a re-examination, where the state or centre decides to apply this. Children still can't be expelled.
Physical punishment and mental harassment of children are prohibited. Teachers who violate this face disciplinary action.
Schools need recognition and must meet norms on buildings, teachers and facilities. Pupil–teacher ratio: 30:1 in Classes 1–5 and 35:1 in Classes 6–8.
Government and aided schools must have a committee — three-quarters parents, with half women — to monitor the school and plan its development.
Complaints about violations go to the local authority, then to the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights.
